thread:
incident-bot: P1 INCIDENT — PrivateConnect path instability detected for customer ACME (asia-south1 <-> eu-west1). Elevated 5xx rate (approx 20%) to inference endpoints started ~1719801200. Pager to oncall.
maya (oncall): @sam I'm on it. Pulling up metrics and routing. Can someone grab the traceroutes from the affected VPC? @rahul please surface customer impact.
sam (net-eng): grabbing traceroute from asia-south1 egress -> eu-west1
sam (net-eng): ```
traceroute to 34.200.10.5 (34.200.10.5), 30 hops max, 60 byte packets
 1  10.0.0.1  0.23 ms  0.21 ms  0.19 ms
 2  100.64.1.5  1.2 ms  1.0 ms  1.1 ms
 3  203.0.113.2  12.5 ms  12.3 ms  12.7 ms
 4  198.51.100.9  34.6 ms  120.4 ms  35.0 ms
 5  * * *
 6  203.0.113.18  220.1 ms  219.9 ms  221.0 ms
 7  34.200.10.5  220.7 ms  220.3 ms  220.8 ms
```
sam (net-eng): see the big latency jump between hop 3 and 6, plus intermittent * on hop 5 — looks like asymmetric pathing and intermittent drops.
maya (oncall): running tcpdump on the service ENI to check for retransmits
maya (oncall): ```
17:05:12.345678 IP 10.0.12.45.51432 > 34.200.10.5.443: Flags [S], seq 0, win 64240, options [mss 1460,sackOK,TS val 123456 ecr 0,nop,wscale 7], length 0
17:05:12.445789 IP 10.0.12.45.51432 > 34.200.10.5.443: Flags [S], seq 0, retransmission, length 0
17:05:12.546890 IP 10.0.12.45.51432 > 34.200.10.5.443: Flags [S], seq 0, retransmission, length 0
```
maya (oncall): SYN retransmits -> likely path loss or MTU/blackhole. Correlates with traceroute gaps.
rahul (prod-support): ACME reporting 502s and webhook timeouts. Their SRE says ~15-20% of requests failing between 17:02-17:15 UTC. They've escalated to their account team. @claire do we have a provider contact yet?
claire (cloud-liaison): opened ticket with carrier (ticket 987654). Provider reports a fabric flap in eu-west1 pop at 17:04 UTC affecting some PrivateConnect circuits. They're investigating BGP session churn. Will share updates in carrier ticket.
sam (net-eng): looking at BGP RIB snapshots — seeing AS path oscillation: several prefixes are switching between direct path (AS64500) and partner transit (AS65555) with prepends added.
sam (net-eng): ```
BGP> show ip bgp 34.200.0.0/16
*> 34.200.0.0/16    203.0.113.2 from 203.0.113.2 (via AS64500)  valid, external, best
  34.200.0.0/16    198.51.100.15 from 198.51.100.15 (via AS65555)  external
```
maya (oncall): mitigation options: 1) request carrier to pin the session / withdraw prepends (slow), 2) failover customer traffic to VPC peering route (fast), 3) advertise more-specific routes from our side to influence path (risky). Recommend tmp peering fallback for ACME while provider stabilizes.
rahul (prod-support): ACME approves fallback peering, wants ETA under 30m and rollback plan.
maya (oncall): starting peering fallback now. Steps: create static route in customer's route table pointing 34.200.0.0/16 -> peering attachment, update security groups for egress, and adjust NAT if needed.
maya (oncall): command snippet (cloud CLI):
```bash
# create route pointing to peering
cloudctl routes create --vpc vpc-0acme --cidr 34.200.0.0/16 --target vpc-peering-attach-1234
# confirm route
cloudctl routes get --vpc vpc-0acme | grep 34.200.0.0
```
deploy-bot: Started deployment: route-change v2 for vpc-0acme by maya at 17:09 UTC
maya (oncall): route applied. Running quick smoke.
maya (oncall): smoke results: 200 responses for 1k requests over 2m, p95 latency 120ms — much improved vs 5xx.
rahul (prod-support): relaying to ACME: "We implemented a temporary VPC peering fallback to bypass the affected carrier path. Your traffic should be stable now. We will keep you posted and rollback after carrier confirms fix." Customer acknowledges :thumbsup:
claire (cloud-liaison): carrier update: they identified and isolated a flapping cross-connect, applying corrective fix. Estimated stabilization in 30-45m. Ticket 987654 -> update #2.
maya (oncall): monitoring: error rate back down to baseline (<=1%). Rolling observation window for 30m. Scheduling handoff.
maya (oncall): Handoff to lee (oncall) at 17:30 UTC — leave notes: peering fallback in place, carrier ticket 987654, rollback plan is to remove peering route and re-enable PrivateConnect path once carrier confirms AS path stable for 15m.
lee (oncall): acked, taking over. If carrier signals clear, I'll coordinate rollback and run canary tests. @sam please keep BGP log collection for the postmortem.
sam (net-eng): saving BGP RIBs and traceroutes. Captured churn between 17:02-17:10. Will attach to incident timeline.
maya (oncall): RESOLVED (mitigated): traffic restored 17:10 UTC via peering fallback. Marking as mitigated; will open incident postmortem and notify account team. Root cause likely carrier fabric flap causing BGP path oscillation and transit prepends -> asymmetric routing + packet loss.
rahul (prod-support): customer update sent. No data exfil suspected. Logged impact window 17:02-17:10, peak 17:04-17:06. Affected calls: model inference endpoints and webhooks. Estimated customers impacted: 1 primary ACME account (multi-tenant endpoints, small % of total traffic).
claire (cloud-liaison): provider confirms stabilization at 17:20 UTC and will monitor for 1h. They will remove the temporary prepends and close ticket after 1h stable.
lee (oncall): I'll keep watches on metrics and confirm rollback plan at ~17:45 UTC. Assigning postmortem to sam and maya. Thanks all for quick response. :raised_hands:
incident-bot: Incident mitigated — P1 -> mitigated at 1719801700. Postmortem ticket: PM-2026-045 assigned.
